newsitem.title: FRANCE: France raises Rushdie case in talks with Iranian.
newsitem.headline: France raises Rushdie case in talks with Iranian.

text.p: France said it renewed a plea to Iran on Thursday that it lift a seven-year-old death sentence against British author Salman Rushdie for his novel "The Satanic Verses", but Paris gave no indication that progress was made.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said the issue was raised during a visit to Paris by Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Mahmoud Vaezi.

Doutriaux, describing Vaezi's visit as routine, said Rushdie's plight had been raised during his talks with French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette and senior ministry official Bertrand Fourcq on Thursday morning.
"We raised this matter very forcefully. There is no doubt about France and Europe's determination on this issue," Doutriaux told reporters at a regular ministry briefing.
The talks touched on a wide array of bilateral, regional and international issues involving France, the European Union and Iran, the French spokesman said.

While the United States has urged the international community to isolate Iran, contending it plays host to Islamic fundamentalists bent on destabilising governments in North Africa and the Middle East, the European Union has opened what it calls a "critical dialogue" with Tehran in hopes of achieving its policy aims.
A key aim of the dialogue has been to convince Iran to lift the death sentence against Rushdie.
